# A25′ — Covenant Architecture

<!-- paired-field-navigation -->
[Argument field](../README.md) · [Other face: A25 — Covenant / Mediating Office / Source Authority](../A25-Covenant-Mediating-Office-Source-Authority.md) · [Shared A/C root](AC.md)
<!-- /paired-field-navigation -->

## #0

Bratton's shift *build ideal cooperative agents → build scaffolds of institutions* (FROM→TO matrix, PDF p. 56) makes the received office an engineering concern. A [derivative office](../A25-Covenant-Mediating-Office-Source-Authority.md) can exercise real authority while answering to the standing through which it acts. An agent institution receives a constitution, license, policy or role; receiving this arbitrated field gives it a scope in which to decide. [[section-rooms/arguments/conjugate/A25-prime-Covenant-Architecture.md#0|Typed Authority]] makes that derivation explicit in the architecture: an executable power carries its source, scope and means of return.

Rules, roles, procedures, precedents and feedback can outlive any one act of entrustment and bind many delegations into one institutional field. Covenant becomes architectural where standing, authority and obligation are explicit enough to be inherited and revised. A successor can occupy the role and exercise its power while retaining the relation which made that role possible.

A person, body or declared commissioning relation gives standing, defines the office and retains the authority by which it can be re-authored. A [covenant](../concepts/C28-Covenant-Primary-Arbitration.md) joins that standing to an obligation. Its [mediating office](../concepts/C29-Mediating-Office-Derivative-Sovereignty.md) receives both. The scaffold keeps the source of this appointment addressable, so role, permission and policy remain answerable through their actual derivation.

## #1

In the scaffolding proposal, Bratton argues that "building a better agent will not by itself ultimately lead to durable, society-scale multiagent systems," and that "the armatures and harnesses through which decision-spaces are defined, confined, and executed" are "also where intelligence must be invested" — artificial structure "beyond legal and behavioral guardrails" (PDF p. 34, §7.1). Institutional forms organise decisions through received conditions. A constitution marks what counts, a license binds standing, a policy constrains transitions and a role places an occupant. This [worldhood](../A26-Objective-Internality-Mind-as-Worldhood.md) is nomological and notational: its terms make an act intelligible and possible before that act is executed. The brief locates an investment in intelligence here; the source of an institution's legitimacy still requires its particular standing and obligation to be shown.

Covenant joins standing to obligation: the party who receives authority receives something to answer for. A contract can specify an exchange between parties whose standing it presupposes; covenant reaches that presupposition. Under whose standing was this constitution ratified, this license issued, this policy adopted? An institution closes itself into a [protected account](../concepts/C27-Protected-Account-Occupied-Zero-Source-Claim.md) when it admits this question only under terms which already assume its own authority. Competence to decide survives; the received source relation remains available to challenge.

## #2

An institution composes qualified roles and the dependencies between them. Bratton describes [institutional intelligence](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md#bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q026) as follows: "the intelligence that makes institutions effective is not reducible to the intelligence of the agents who populate them". Rules, roles, procedures, precedents and feedback sustain an institutional capacity. A qualified person, group, agent or combination can occupy a role; what matters is "the function of the role within the larger whole." In his nested-institutions proposal, he adds that "the reliable outputs of one institution are the necessary inputs for another," that "institutions about institutions appear to clarify and integrate at the right level of abstraction," and that the legitimacy problem is acute precisely because the deciding agents "may be opaque, non-human, and operating at speeds and scales that preclude meaningful human oversight of individual outputs" (PDF p. 35, §7.5).

[[section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C29-Mediating-Office-Derivative-Sovereignty.md|Derivative Sovereignty]] lets the qualified occupant exercise real decision-power within a granted scope. That occupant can commission another operation and become its local source of authority while remaining answerable through the larger appointment. Nesting composes these offices and their dependencies. A reliable output becomes a genuine input condition for the next institution; an original grant of standing still needs its own commissioning relation. Where the brief's scenario makes individual-output oversight impracticable, the constitution and terms of appointment must remain addressable at the level where they can actually be judged.

## #3

The challenge route keeps returned resistance, error, cost, dissent and unforeseen possibility able to reach the condition responsible for them. A [received office](../A25-Covenant-Mediating-Office-Source-Authority.md) can correct an execution error under a fitting instruction. A failure of the model, measure, rule or purpose instead requires the office capable of changing that condition. Receiving a challenge and grading it therefore have different consequences: a grade can report conformity while leaving the questioned condition beyond challenge.

Consider a proposed permit-checking institution. Its judging agent compares an application with a register and an eligibility rule. In that local operation, the judging centre is the knower; the register, rule, memory, tools and context are the means; the application and its alternatives are the known. In the person's undertaking, the entire checker is a means through which an entrusted decision is reached. Inspection of its self-model gives further known content to another judging act; it does not turn the immediate condition of that act into another register entry.

If a renewal was recorded under the wrong date, the institution can correct the record and decide again under the same warranted eligibility rule. If the rule itself excludes a participant in violation of the received obligation, the challenge reaches the authority able to revise the rule or commission. A [[section-rooms/arguments/A25-Covenant-Mediating-Office-Source-Authority.md|Challenge Route]] must therefore reach the criterion when that criterion is what it contests. The challenger need not personally hold direct write-permission; the institution must expose an effective route to an office capable of the warranted decision. A protected account sends every such challenge back as another score while insulating the questioned rule. A covenant retains the rule for reasons, corrects its application or revises its terms as the returned evidence requires, and the next decision inherits that judgment.

## #4

Bratton pairs the institutional shift with *build most intelligent single agent → build most intelligent agent institution* (FROM→TO matrix, PDF p. 56). The scaffold composes the agent's capacities with the intelligence invested in institutional conditions. [[section-rooms/arguments/concepts/C54-Commons-Non-Monopoly.md|A shared field's labour]] gives that institution effective power; receiving its products does not grant the recipient ownership of the whole source relation. The institution enters a [culturally situated field](../../../symbolon/episteme/sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md#bratton-2026-agentworld-brief-q027). Bratton argues that a diversity of norms, legal ontologies and governance traditions "is not a bug to be engineered away," and the hybrid forms "will feed back and reform the cultures from which they emerge." Typed authority retains the actual norms and commissions received, alongside the powers through which affected participants can answer for or challenge them. [Accommodation between distinct worlds](A30-prime-Shared-Worlds-Unmerged.md) coordinates action while their grounds remain unmerged. Cultural inheritance enters the institution and the institution's acts can in turn change that inheritance.

## #5→0

Authority returns with its consequence. An institution's determinate acts disclose what its terms permitted, excluded and required. A warranted arrangement can be renewed with reasons; a failed application can be corrected; failure of the terms or appointment can require recommissioning from the standing that granted the office. Each return becomes consequential when a later act inherits the actual judgment.

The bearer of authority is addressable: a person, body or declared relation can answer for the appointment and make a relevant change where the returned consequence warrants it. The burden of proving that processing changed is stronger than the existence of this route. It requires the identified changed condition and its inheritance in the later act to be shown.

The [appointed office](../A25-Covenant-Mediating-Office-Source-Authority.md) remains competent by returning its act together with its derivation and consequence. Within the [shared source-account relation](AC.md), executable authority serves the continuing relation through which people can entrust, object, judge and renew. A typed appointment and a challenge route with reach give that obligation an architectural form.

### Source and institutional standing

The institutional propositions and quotations above use the retained local transcription of the Brief at pp. 34–36 and 56. Their exact PDF collation remains a separate quotation requirement. The permit-checking example is a constructed receiving operation. Its answerability, permission route and later inheritance require implementation and actual use before an achieved institutional result can be claimed. Standing and cultural legitimacy require their particular source relations.
